_meta.source: Export restrictions on record, IFPRI Food and Fertilizer Export Restrictions Tracker pattern; every entry re-verified on 2026-09-16 against the primary notification or a wire report, cited per row
_meta.notes: Statuses: official (a government notification in force), reported (a measure reported in force by a wire source), historical (lifted or window closed, kept on record). Exposure (who is hit) is computed live from the atlas by restrictionExposure() and is real regardless of status. No entry without a source_url. The IFPRI tracker itself has no downloadable table (checked 2026-09-16: Shiny app and API only), so verification runs against primary sources. Next review due after 30 days.

data.source_name: DGFT notification of 13 May 2026, reported by Business Standard, 14 May 2026
data.note: Sugar export policy moved from restricted to prohibited with immediate effect through 30 September 2026, on domestic stock concerns. EU and US tariff-rate quota shipments, advance-authorisation and pipeline cargoes are exempt. In force on the review date, 16 September 2026.

Domestic market obligation: export permits tied to domestic sales, in place since the 2022 ban was lifted and tightened from 12 December 2025 (35 percent of the obligation volume through state-owned firms), with Permendag 16/2026 moving toward state-only export permits by 2027 ahead of the B50 biodiesel mandate. A standing permit regime, not a ban.

data.source_name: DGFT Notification 20/2023-24; lifting reported by IFPRI, 2024
data.note: Ban on non-basmati white rice exports from 20 July 2023. Lifted 28 September 2024 for a 490 dollar per tonne minimum export price, itself removed 20 October 2024. India's 2025 rice exports reached about 21.5 Mt with the curbs gone. Nothing comparable in force on 16 September 2026.

Outright ban on palm oil and cooking oil exports from 28 April 2022, revoked from 23 May 2022 by Regulation 30/2022. The domestic market obligation that replaced it is the separate reported entry above.

data.source_name: Government of Russia decree (2026 quota); earlier years via Interfax
data.note: Tariff-rate export quota each 15 February to 30 June since 2021: 24 to 29 Mt in 2024, 11 Mt in 2025, 20 Mt in 2026. The 2026 window closed on 30 June. From 1 September 2026 the wheat, barley and corn export duty is set to zero through year end (Bloomberg, 2 September 2026), an easing, not a restriction.

Exports restricted beyond 31 October 2023 for an indefinite period on lower cane output; 1 Mt allowed for 2024-25 and 1.5 Mt for 2025-26. Superseded by the outright prohibition of 13 May 2026, the official entry above.
